children: The S&P 500 (
) closed in the green on Friday, after the week saw latest payroll data and earnings reports from Micron and Accenture.
Nasdaq
rose marginally for the week, led by Lumentum Holdings (
), which advanced over 15%. Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:
HSBC says Target’s turnaround ‘gaining momentum’
HSBC
Target
to Buy from Hold and raised its price target to $190 from $125, saying the company’s turnaround is "gaining momentum" and has further room to run.

Analyst Joe Thomas said second-quarter sales performance was "encouraging" and suggested the store base was not being “unduly cannibalised.”  Thomas added improvements in Beauty, Food and Beverage, Hardlines, and Household Essentials were beginning to resonate, although Apparel and Home still require further work.
HSBC raised its FY27 EPS estimate to $10.61 from $8.26 and said forecasts “look conservative.”
Moderna downgraded on
‘unjustifiable’ valuation
Citi
Moderna
to Sell from Neutral, citing an "unjustifiable" valuation following a late-stage trial win for its personalized cancer shot, intismeran autogene, developed with Merck

Analyst Geoff Meacham noted that since the Phase 3 win in melanoma last August, the Massachusetts-based biotech has rallied more than 222% compared with a 2% decline in its peers as represented by the State Street SPDR S&P Biotech ETF

“While intismeran could become a market-leading therapy in melanoma, we believe the re-rating now reflects successful expansion in many tumor types and unrealistic implied sales,” Meacham wrote, lowering his PT to $60 from $80 per share.
Deutsche Bank turns bearish on PepsiCo
Deutsche Bank downgraded PepsiCo
to Hold from Buy on the view that a turnaround scenario is now complicated.
Analyst Steve Powers acknowledged the low valuation on PepsiCo

but noted the firm now has less certainty in the company's strategic direction in North America and less conviction in its ability to deliver a durable recovery in the PepsiCo Foods North America segment.
Occidental Petroleum raised to Buy on strong debt reduction
Goldman Sachs upgraded Occidental Petroleum

to Buy from Neutral with a $69 price target, bumped up from $63, citing the company's differentiated advanced recovery approach, strong outlook for debt reduction and dividend growth potential, targeted $4B cash flow improvement by 2030, and an attractive risk/reward skew given the current discounted valuation.
Goldman's Neil Mehta said he has seen strong YTD share price performance from the bank's oil E&P coverage given an elevated oil pricing environment, with Occidental

shares trading in line with the broader coverage despite "structural improvements that OXY has driven across its business through an incremental focus on capital efficiency and deleveraging" under new CEO Richard Jackson.
Mehta double-downgraded Tourmaline Oil
to Sell from Buy with a C$49 price target, cut from C$59, citing a challenging Western Canadian natural gas macro environment in the near-term.
Wells Fargo upgraded
Consolidated Edison
to Overweight from Equal Weight with a $118 price target, raised from $108, viewing the stock as a "defensive diversification away from the broader AI trade."
Wells Fargo upgraded
BP
to Overweight from Equal Weight with a $57 price target, raised from $48, while downgrading
ExxonMobil
to Equal Weight from Overweight with an unchanged $182 PT, saying relative valuations are "converging in BP's favor," helped by faster debt reduction and resource development.
Nvidia
was in focus as Morgan Stanley reinstated the Jensen Huang-led tech giant as its top pick in the semiconductor space.

“Nvidia remains very early in the ramp of a new product cycle, powered shell constraints play into Nvidia’s strengths, and recent agentic enthusiasm can accelerate Vera adoption,” Morgan Stanley analysts, led by Joseph Moore, wrote.

title: Notable analyst calls this week: Target, Moderna and PepsiCo among top picks
